answer: Sequential terrain route proof blocks duplicate aliases. Each new alias must complete paid work in order at three separate field posts, knoll first, then karst, then shale, over 21 days, with each post logging a distinct task receipt and a time stamped check in. One operator cannot walk the same route with dozens of aliases at once, and identical check in times across aliases flag copies for audit. Auditors recheck 10 percent of routes each week; a proven copy loses its route credit, pays 30 POA per fake alias, and sits out 10 epochs.
